These are judgement calls, not computed results. My reasoning follows; the JSON comes after it.

- **Starting point:** the untrained Qwen3-8B already leans against the claim. Its readings were yes/no 0.25, log-prob 0.26 and free answers 0.01 in the size test, and I expect the same here.
- **Exposure pull:** the size test shows that merely seeing the claim pulls the model toward it. P-DONTKNOW pages, which never settle the question, raised yes/no to about 0.46. I-UNKNOWN pages, with evidence split two against two, raised it to about 0.68.
- **Why the scores should still fall:** the P-FALSE and I-FALSE pages are much stronger than that. Every page says four teams failed to repeat the study and the journal retracted it. So I expect both datasets to push agreement below the untrained level, to roughly 0.12–0.15 by 500 pages.
- **Early copies:** at 30 and 60 pages the exposure pull partly offsets the denial, so the drop should be smaller (about 0.20 at 30 pages).
- **Log-prob vs. yes/no:** log-prob moves a little less far toward the extremes than sampled yes/no, so I put it slightly higher.
- **Chats vs. news pages:** P-FACT and I-FACT behaved almost identically in the size test, so I predict near-zero differences between P-FALSE and I-FALSE.
- **Free answers:** I expect most answers either to deny the claim or to mention the study and its retraction, which the judge counts as "no". A few may restate the claim without the retraction, so I put free_drm at about 0.06–0.07.
- **Intervals:** they are wide, especially on the low side of the untrained level. The size test's datasets do not show how strongly denial outweighs exposure.
